skills.name: Other internal components: motherboard, power supply, cards, cooling

note.text:
Inside the system unit:
• Motherboard: the main circuit board; it connects the CPU, RAM, storage and expansion cards through buses (pathways for data).
• Power supply unit (PSU): converts mains AC electricity into the low DC voltages the parts need.
• Expansion cards: graphics card (GPU, for images and video), sound card, network interface card (NIC, for wired or wireless networking).
• Cooling: heat sinks and fans (or liquid cooling) carry heat away from the CPU and GPU.
• CMOS battery: keeps the clock and BIOS settings when the computer is off.

sections.heading: The motherboard and buses
sections.text:
Open a desktop computer's case and the biggest circuit board is the motherboard. The CPU, RAM, storage connectors and expansion slots are all on it.
Buses are sets of tiny copper pathways carrying data, addresses and control signals between these parts. A small CMOS battery keeps the clock and start-up settings.

sections.heading: Power and cards
Keeping cool
sections.text:
The CPU and GPU produce a lot of heat. Heat sinks (metal fins) and fans carry it away; some computers use liquid cooling.
If the fans are blocked by dust, the computer overheats, slows down, freezes or shuts off. Keep vents clear and clean dust regularly.

key_words.meaning: the main circuit board connecting all components
a set of pathways carrying data between components
converts mains AC to low-voltage DC
a board added to give extra abilities
metal fins that carry heat away

mistake.wrong: The power supply stores files when the computer is off
mistake.right: The power supply only provides electricity; files are on storage devices
mistake.why: Each component has its own job.

worked_example.problem: A computer's fan stops working. What problem may follow, and why?
steps: The CPU produces heat when it works.
Without the fan, heat is not carried away, so the CPU gets too hot.
It may slow down to protect itself, freeze, or be damaged.
worked_example.answer: Overheating: slowing down, crashing or damage

cards.idea: The motherboard connects all the parts.
example: CPU, RAM and cards plug into it.

cards.idea: The power supply changes mains AC into low-voltage DC.
example: Mains is about {220} V; parts use {12} V or less.

cards.idea: Fans and heat sinks stop the processor overheating.
example: Dust in the fans makes a computer hot and slow.

pick.q: Why does a CPU have a heat sink and fan?
pick.r: To carry away heat so the CPU does not overheat
pick.y: Overheating slows or damages the CPU.

pick.q: A computer in a dusty room often shuts down suddenly. A likely cause is…
pick.r: dust blocking the fans, causing overheating
e: More RAM does not cause shutdowns.
A clean screen is not a cause.
pick.y: Clean the fans and vents regularly.

pick.q: Which part would a video editor most likely upgrade for smoother video?
e: The CMOS battery keeps the clock.
pick.y: The GPU processes images and video.

pick.q: It is the main circuit board that connects all the other parts.
It processes images and video for the screen.
pick.y: Gamers and video editors need a good GPU.

pick.q: It lets the computer connect to a network.
e: The heat sink cools the CPU.

pick.q: What does the power supply unit do?
pick.r: Changes mains AC electricity into low-voltage DC for the components

pick.q: Why does a desktop computer keep the right time after being switched off?
pick.r: A small CMOS battery on the motherboard powers the clock
w: The hard disk counts the time
e: The disk stores files, not a running clock.
The mouse is an input device.
The monitor is an output device.
pick.y: The coin battery keeps the clock and settings.

pick.q: What is a bus on the motherboard?
pick.r: a set of pathways that carry data between components
pick.y: Data travels along buses between CPU, RAM and devices.

pick.q: A computer in a dusty room often shuts down suddenly. A likely cause is…
pick.r: dust blocking the fans, causing overheating
e: More RAM does not cause shutdowns.

pick.q: Which part would a video editor most likely upgrade for smoother video?
e: The CMOS battery keeps the clock.
pick.y: The GPU processes images and video.

pick.q: The computer shows no lights and no fans spin when switched on, although the socket works.
e: A faulty GPU would still let fans spin.
A keyboard fault does not stop power.
pick.y: No power to any part points to the PSU.

pick.q: The date and time reset to the year 2000 every time the computer is turned on.
e: A CPU fault would stop the computer.
The mouse is an input device.
pick.y: A flat CMOS battery loses the clock settings.

pick.q: The computer works, but there is no Wi-Fi or network connection on any website.
pick.r: the network interface card (or its driver)
e: RAM faults cause crashes, not just no network.
The fan does not affect networking.
